title: Meta Muse Voice Now Available for US Video Chat
summary: Meta rolls out Muse Voice video chat nationwide, letting US users talk face-to-face with customizable AI avatars powered by new realtime models.
body_markdown:
#### 💡 TL;DR


- Meta launched Muse Voice nationwide in the US, enabling video calls with customizable AI avatars using new realtime models.
- Users can personalize their Muse avatar to resemble people, animals, or characters, with subtle gestures matching conversation tone.
- The feature arrives ahead of Meta's year-end Muse Charm wearable device and extends to mobile, web, Mac, and AI Glasses.


Meta announced on November 5, 2026 that Muse Voice, its video chat feature for the Muse AI agent, is now available to all US users. The rollout brings live, face-to-face conversations with customizable AI avatars to mobile, web, and Mac platforms, positioning Meta's consumer AI offering against voice-only competitors like ChatGPT Voice and Google Assistant.


## What Muse Voice Delivers


Muse Voice introduces two new AI models: Muse Realtime Avatar and Muse Realtime Voice. Together, these technologies power an animated avatar nicknamed Jolly that responds to user questions and task requests in real time. Unlike text-based or voice-only AI assistants, Muse Voice provides a visual persona that uses subtle facial expressions and hand gestures synchronized to the conversation's tone.


Users can customize their Muse avatar to resemble a person, animal, or fictional character. Meta's design philosophy centers on anthropomorphization, betting that giving the AI agent a visible personality will strengthen user engagement and emotional connection during extended interactions.


## Release Date and Availability


Officially launched on November 5, 2026, Muse Voice completes a rollout first previewed at Meta's Connect developer conference in September 2026. Meta chief AI officer Alexandr Wang confirmed the nationwide availability in a blog post and on X, sharing a demo video of his own Muse avatar, a fluffy white dog, offering tongue-in-cheek advice about meme-posting etiquette.


The feature is currently live on mobile devices, web browsers, and macOS. Meta confirmed that Muse Voice will extend to its AI Glasses and the upcoming Muse Charm wearable device, a Tamagotchi-style gadget expected before year-end that will display the avatar on a small screen.


## How It Compares to Competitors


While OpenAI's ChatGPT and Google's Gemini offer voice interaction, neither provides a persistent visual avatar during calls. Meta's approach differentiates Muse by adding a visual layer to conversational AI, a strategy the company believes will drive longer, more frequent engagement.


- Muse Voice supports real-time video calls with customizable avatars
- Competitors focus on voice-only or text-based interactions
- Meta's avatar uses dynamic expressions tied to conversational context
- Integration with upcoming Muse Charm hardware extends the experience beyond screens


## Hardware Integration on the Horizon


Meta plans to ship the Muse Charm wearable device by the end of 2026. The pocket-sized gadget will feature a small display showing the user's chosen Muse avatar, enabling on-the-go conversations without pulling out a phone. The device represents Meta's push into dedicated AI hardware, competing with products like the Rabbit R1 and Humane AI Pin.


Meta has not disclosed pricing or exact release timing for the Muse Charm, but the company confirmed it will work seamlessly with the same Muse Voice models powering the mobile and desktop experience.


## What This Means


Meta's Muse Voice launch signals the company's commitment to building a differentiated consumer AI experience through visual engagement and cross-device integration. By combining real-time avatar technology with an upcoming wearable form factor, Meta is betting that users will prefer AI agents with personality and presence over disembodied voices. The success of this strategy will depend on whether customizable avatars drive sustained usage or become a novelty feature. Either way, Muse Voice establishes a new baseline for conversational AI interfaces heading into 2027.
